Added bundle update --bundler step in Dockerfile to automatically
update lockfile to match installed Bundler version (4.0.0).

This fix:
- Resolves GitHub Actions 'Build (Latest Deps)' workflow failure
- Maintains all gem versions from Gemfile.lock (only Bundler updates)
- Aligns with project's zero version pin philosophy
- Ensures compatibility without requiring manual lockfile regeneration

Fixes: Bundler version conflict (4.0.0 vs ~> 2.3)

author: bamr87
subject: fix(docker): remove bundle update --bundler that requires existing bundle
body:
The previous fix attempted to run 'bundle update --bundler' before
'bundle install', which fails with error:
'This Bundle hasn't been installed yet. Run bundle install'

Bundler 4.0 can successfully read and process lockfiles created by
Bundler 2.x without requiring an explicit update step.

This fix:
- Removes the premature 'bundle update --bundler' step
- Relies on Bundler 4.0's backward compatibility
- Allows bundle install to proceed with 2.x lockfile
- Maintains all gem versions from Gemfile.lock

Resolves: GitHub Actions CI build failure (exit code 22)

author: bamr87
subject: fix(docker): install bundler 2.3 to match Gemfile.lock requirement
body:
- Install bundler ~> 2.3 instead of latest 4.0.0
- Matches BUNDLED WITH 2.3.25 in Gemfile.lock
- Satisfies gemspec dependency constraint: bundler (~> 2.3)
- Fixes 'version solving has failed' error in Docker build

The Gemfile.lock requires bundler ~> 2.3, but our Dockerfile
was installing the latest version (4.0.0). While Bundler 4.0
can technically read 2.x lockfiles, it doesn't satisfy the
version constraint check during dependency resolution.

author: bamr87
subject: fix(deps): commit Gemfile.lock for reproducible builds
body:
- Remove Gemfile.lock from .gitignore
- Commit lockfile with github-pages 232 (latest)
- Ensures Docker builds use tested dependency versions
- Fixes CI failure with rdiscount 2.1.7 compilation error

Root cause: Without committed lockfile, Docker's bundle install
resolved dependencies fresh, picking old github-pages v28 which
depends on rdiscount 2.1.7 that won't compile with GCC 13+.

With lockfile committed, Docker will use github-pages 232 which
doesn't have the rdiscount dependency.

This aligns with zero-pin philosophy:
- Gemfile has no pins (allows updates)
- Gemfile.lock captures what actually works
- CI validates before production
- Production gets exactly what passed tests

author: bamr87
subject: fix(docker): pin Ruby 3.3 and update dependencies in test-latest workflow
body:
Problem: Build failing with Ruby 3.4 (latest) due to incompatibility with
native C extensions in older gems. The posix-spawn gem (0.3.15) required by
github-pages v39 fails to compile on Ruby 3.4 due to API changes.

Root Causes:
1. Gemfile.lock contains ancient dependencies (github-pages v39 from 2015)
2. Ruby :latest (3.4) breaks compatibility with many native extensions
3. test-latest workflow wasn't actually updating dependencies before building

Solutions Implemented:
1. Pin Ruby to 3.3-slim in Dockerfile (all stages)
   - Aligns with CI test matrix (Ruby 3.2, 3.3)
   - Stable gem ecosystem compatibility
   - Will upgrade to 3.4 once gems are compatible

2. Add dependency update step in test-latest workflow
   - Runs 'bundle update --all' before building
   - Now truly tests with latest compatible versions
   - Uses same Ruby 3.3 for consistency

3. Enhanced documentation in Dockerfile
   - Explains Ruby version strategy
   - Documents why we don't use :latest

How to Avoid This Issue:
- Always test Docker builds in CI before upgrading Ruby major versions
- Pin Ruby to tested versions (match CI matrix)
- Run 'bundle update' regularly to keep dependencies current
- Monitor Ruby release notes for breaking changes in native extensions
- Use test-latest workflow to catch breakages early

Technical Details:
- Ruby 3.4 changed rb_hash_foreach signature (VALUE vs specific types)
- Old gems like posix-spawn (0.3.15) not updated for Ruby 3.4
- Modern gems (github-pages 232+) hand…
